nodes.label: ADR-001: Keep A Monorepo Initially
nodes.rationale: Keeping /front and /back in one repo supports gradual migration and avoids splitting the project before a clear API boundary exists.

nodes.label: ADR-008: Frontend Framework (Vue 3 + Bootstrap 5, proposed)
nodes.rationale: No Vue/React was detected in the initial audit; adopting Vue must be treated as a real Blade-to-SPA migration, not a file move.

nodes.label: Migration Hygiene Rules
nodes.rationale: Meaningful behavior changes must be recorded in the migration log and new risks in pending risks, so future sessions have a reliable trail.

nodes.label: SEC-002: Global Legacy IoT API Key
nodes.norm_label: sec-002: global legacy iot api key
nodes.rationale: Ingestion still accepts a global legacy API_KEY besides per-device keys; if leaked it could inject readings into any active sensor. Recommendation: rely on per-device keys and retire the global key.

nodes.label: SEC-004: SMTP Password Stored as System Setting
nodes.norm_label: sec-004: smtp password stored as system setting
nodes.rationale: SMTP password is never returned via API but is stored in system_settings; direct DB access would expose it. Recommendation: encrypt sensitive SystemSetting values or move them to environment/secret manager.

nodes.label: Incremental Migration Principle

nodes.label: Front/Back Separation Goal
nodes.rationale: Target is a modern SPA in /front consuming only backend APIs, with /back as Laravel REST+Broadcasting, so frontend never depends on Blade, Laravel helpers, or direct DB access.

nodes.label: ADR-002: Backend As REST API + Broadcasting
nodes.norm_label: adr-002: backend as rest api + broadcasting
nodes.rationale: Allows the frontend to run independently and prepares the backend for later modularization or service extraction.

nodes.label: ADR-004: Incremental Migration
nodes.rationale: Complete and normalize APIs first, then create the frontend, then retire Blade gradually to reduce the risk of breaking existing behavior.

nodes.label: Eloquent::update() bulk calls do not fire observers
nodes.community_name: audit.md — architecture audit and implementation plan
nodes.norm_label: eloquent::update() bulk calls do not fire observers
nodes.rationale: Laravel mass updates bypass individual model events, so resolveAll()-style bulk resolution does not trigger AlertObserver; alert resolution/device status therefore not fully event-driven.

nodes.label: Frontend realtime model (shared Echo instance)
nodes.community_name: audit.md — architecture audit and implementation plan
nodes.rationale: One Echo/Pusher-JS connection is meant to be reused across the SPA (not one per component) to avoid duplicate socket overhead; polling timers exist alongside it as legacy fallback duplicating the same state.

nodes.label: No-polling gate (definition of done)
nodes.community_name: audit.md — architecture audit and implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Verified via source inspection plus browser network traces, transport restriction checks and backend relay/worker inspection — a passing build or simulated handler test alone is explicitly insufficient evidence.

nodes.label: Observer/Event side-effect convention
nodes.community_name: audit.md — architecture audit and implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Business-rule side effects (alert evaluation, email, broadcast) belong in Observers/Listeners, not controllers, to keep controllers thin and side effects consistent across ingestion paths.

nodes.label: Transactional outbox + binlog-driven CDC relay
nodes.community_name: audit.md — architecture audit and implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Recommended over best-effort dual write (DB insert then XADD) and over SQL-polling outbox, because it satisfies durable delivery while respecting the strict no-periodic-state-discovery-polling constraint; requires a deployment feasibility gate (binlog connector/sink verification) before rollout.

nodes.label: Cursor/replay + snapshot recovery protocol
nodes.community_name: audit.md — architecture audit and implementation plan
nodes.rationale: Proposed WebSocket-only recovery: buffer live events during snapshot boundary, send bounded resume command with scoped cursor, replay authorized events with recovery-complete watermark, or fall back to DB snapshot + catch-up if cursor expired; polling explicitly excluded as an acceptable recovery mechanism, must precede timer deletion (G0-P10 rollout gates).

nodes.label: Laravel Sanctum
nodes.community_name: ADR-009: SPA Auth Uses Sanctum Bearer Tokens Initially

nodes.label: Authentication Strategy: Sanctum Bearer Tokens
nodes.community_name: ADR-009: SPA Auth Uses Sanctum Bearer Tokens Initially

nodes.label: ADR-009: SPA Auth Uses Sanctum Bearer Tokens Initially
nodes.community_name: ADR-009: SPA Auth Uses Sanctum Bearer Tokens Initially
nodes.norm_label: adr-009: spa auth uses sanctum bearer tokens initially
nodes.rationale: Continuing the existing Sanctum Bearer token path completes Phase 1 with smaller risk than switching immediately to cookie-based Sanctum SPA auth, which needs coordinated CORS/CSRF/cookie-domain changes; frontend token storage strategy must be revisited in Phase 3 to reduce XSS impact.

nodes.label: Bearer Token in localStorage Risk
nodes.community_name: ADR-009: SPA Auth Uses Sanctum Bearer Tokens Initially
nodes.rationale: Token Bearer stored in localStorage keeps XSS impact higher than an HttpOnly cookie strategy; functional but a known tradeoff from ADR-009.

nodes.label: SEC-003: Bearer Token in localStorage
nodes.community_name: ADR-009: SPA Auth Uses Sanctum Bearer Tokens Initially
nodes.rationale: XSS in the frontend could extract the Bearer token; recommendation is to harden CSP and evaluate migrating to Sanctum HttpOnly cookie once the SPA is stable.

nodes.label: ADR-005: Separate Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: Anything bundled into the frontend can be exposed to users, so frontend may only use public VITE_* variables while backend keeps secrets.

nodes.label: ADR-006: API-Only Frontend Communication
nodes.rationale: The frontend must not access the database, internal files, Laravel models, service classes, or backend implementation details directly.

nodes.label: FIX-001: front/.env Configured With Only Public VITE_* Vars
nodes.norm_label: fix-001: front/.env configured with only public vite_* vars
nodes.rationale: Ensures no backend secrets are copied into the frontend bundle, enforcing ADR-005.

nodes.label: SEC-001: Public Telemetry/Operational Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Endpoints like /api/dashboard/public, /api/sensors/{sensor}/latest-readings, /api/devices/{device}/sensors and /api/alerts/active remain unauthenticated for Blade-era compatibility; a third party with network access could read operational state. Recommendation: move to auth:sanctum once the SPA reliably sends Bearer tokens.

nodes.label: FIX-004: Internal Metrics Endpoint Requires auth:sanctum + admin
nodes.norm_label: fix-004: internal metrics endpoint requires auth:sanctum + admin
nodes.rationale: The internal metrics endpoint was previously accessible without admin authentication; guarded to prevent unauthorized operational data exposure.

nodes.label: DashboardMetricsServiceTest constructor non-conformity
nodes.rationale: DashboardMetricsService constructor changed to require AlertService but 3 unit tests were not updated to inject it, causing ArgumentCountError; tracked as an open non-conformity blocking full ISO 9001/12207 quality-control closure.

nodes.label: ICONTEC/ISO alignment (not certification) declaration policy
nodes.rationale: Repository declares technical/documentary alignment with ICONTEC and ISO norms deliberately without claiming formal external certification, since no accredited body audit was performed; every compliance claim must link concrete file/line evidence or a verification command.

nodes.label: SEC-005: Testing APP_KEY Committed in .env.testing
nodes.rationale: Low impact if only used for tests; must never be reused in staging/production.

nodes.label: Alerts table lacks context snapshot
nodes.rationale: alerts table stores only sensor_reading_id/alert_rule_id/resolved, reconstructing severity/message/value via live relations to sensor_readings/alert_rules/sensors/devices/labs; separating the alerts module would require snapshotting this context to avoid dependency on live rows.

nodes.label: Email side effect embedded in Alert model
nodes.norm_label: email side effect embedded in alert model
nodes.rationale: Alert::sendDangerAlertEmail mutates global config() and calls Mail::send from within the model, coupling persistence model to SMTP infrastructure; recommended to move to a dedicated notifier service/job.

nodes.label: mail_enabled toggle not enforced
nodes.rationale: mail_enabled setting exists in config/UI but neither Alert::sendDangerAlertEmail nor NotificationService::notifyDangerAlertByEmail check it, so danger alerts can email even when the toggle is off — identified pain point for module separation.

nodes.label: Polling timers duplicating realtime state
nodes.rationale: AppLayout.vue (10s), ActiveAlertsCard.vue (5s), SensorMonitorBoard.vue (~2s) poll REST endpoints that duplicate what WebSocket events already deliver; targeted for removal only after recovery protocol exists (audit.md TASK-008/009).

nodes.label: Two dynamic mail-configuration styles
nodes.rationale: EmailConfigController::testEmail uses legacy config keys (driver/host/etc) while Alert::sendDangerAlertEmail uses mail.default/mail.from/mail.mailers.smtp — inconsistent dynamic config mutation approaches that can drift.

nodes.label: NewSensorReading::handle() likely dead code
nodes.rationale: NewSensorReading::handle() calls checkForAlert() but the event is never registered as a listener anywhere found, suggesting either dead code or an abandoned earlier design intention.

nodes.label: Alert threshold comparison is inclusive (<=, >=)
nodes.rationale: AlertService threshold check uses belowMin = value <= min_value and aboveMax = value >= max_value, but UI copy describes exclusive comparison ('menor a' / 'supera'), a documented UI/backend mismatch.

nodes.label: Real SMTP credentials in SystemSettingsSeeder
nodes.rationale: database/seeders/SystemSettingsSeeder.php historically carried real-looking SMTP credentials in plain text; flagged as security risk requiring rotation before reuse, blocks safe module separation if replicated as-is.

nodes.label: State ownership target: WS -> Pinia -> components
nodes.norm_label: state ownership target: ws -> pinia -> components
nodes.rationale: Not yet implemented; goal is a single domain-projection state path per screen instead of a fourth parallel component-local polling path.

nodes.label: Echo channel registry / reference-counted subscription ownership
nodes.norm_label: echo channel registry / reference-counted subscription ownership
nodes.rationale: Current useSensorRealtime/useAlertsRealtime call leaveChannel which tears down the entire shared channel for all consumers; proposed fix keeps one Echo connection per tab but reference-counts individual listener subscriptions so one consumer unsubscribing doesn't break others.

nodes.label: Two parallel ingestion paths (legacy + raw)
nodes.rationale: Legacy path persists SensorReading directly and evaluates alerts synchronously via observers; newer raw ingestion path XADDs to Redis Streams iot.raw-events but has no consumer yet, so readings published there do not automatically become SensorReading rows. Kept unmerged deliberately pending consumer implementation.

nodes.label: Raw-first ingestion pipeline architecture
nodes.rationale: Design goal is decoupling: device -> MQTT -> ingestion_service (validate/normalize) -> Laravel persists raw_sensor_events -> publishes reference to Redis Stream iot.raw-events -> future data_jobs_service consumes/transforms/persists processed data and integrates alerts. Publication does not block ingestion if Redis fails; raw persistence is preserved as the durability anchor.
